scan.summary: This is the company's written emergency action plan for the Portland facility covering fire, chemical release, medical emergency, earthquake and other emergencies affecting all 42 employees. It describes alarm systems, evacuation routes and assembly points, headcount procedures, rescue and medical response, and staff training requirements. The plan must comply with OSHA 1910.38 and Oregon OSHA rules.
scan.freshness_note: This document was last revised in February 2021, more than five years ago. A policy like this should be reviewed and updated at least annually. Under the plan's own section 6, the facilities lead reviews it every January, so a 2026 update would be expected and is overdue.

gaps.title: Missing contact name or title for plan information and duties
gaps.description: OSHA 1910.38(c)(6) requires the plan to include the name or job title of every employee who may be contacted by employees who need more information about the plan or an explanation of their duties. This document does not list such names or titles.
gaps.fix: Add a section identifying specific employees (by name or title) who can answer questions about the plan and employee duties—for example, the facilities lead or a safety officer.

gaps.title: Missing procedures for employees remaining to operate critical plant operations
gaps.description: OSHA 1910.38(c)(3) requires the plan to include procedures for employees who remain to operate critical plant operations before they evacuate. This plan does not describe such procedures.
gaps.fix: Add a section describing which employees (if any) are assigned to remain briefly to shut down critical operations, what those operations are, and when and how they must evacuate after shutdown is complete.

gaps.title: Alarm system signals not ANSI-compliant
gaps.description: OSHA 1910.165(b) requires that employee alarm systems use signals complying with ANSI S3.41-1974. The plan describes a continuous horn for evacuation and three short horns for shelter-in-place, but does not confirm these meet the ANSI standard or reference the standard.
gaps.fix: Verify the audible horn signals in the building meet ANSI S3.41-1974 standards, document that verification, and add a reference to the standard in section 2 or as a new compliance note.
gaps.quote: The alarm is tested on the first Monday of each month by the facilities lead. A continuous horn means evacuate. Three short horns repeated means shelter in place because of an outdoor hazard.

gaps.title: Plan not reviewed or updated since February 2021
gaps.description: Oregon OSHA rule 437-002-0042 and OSHA 1910.38(f) require the plan to be reviewed with employees when it is changed, when an employee's responsibilities change, and the facilities lead states in section 6 that the plan is reviewed every January. The document is over five years old with no update date shown.
gaps.fix: Conduct the required January annual review and issue a revised plan dated with the current year. Update evacuation maps, floor warden roster, and verify that all procedures remain current with any facility or staffing changes.
gaps.locator: Section 6, page 5; header shows Revised February 2021
gaps.quote: The facilities lead reviews the plan every January and updates the evacuation maps whenever the building layout changes.

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence in document identification and content reading. Gaps are clearly based on OSHA 1910.38(c) requirements, which I confirmed via web search. The plan itself is well-written and covers most OSHA minimum elements, but three substantive gaps exist: (1) no named contact for plan questions (1910.38(c)(6)), (2) no procedures for critical operations shutdown (1910.38(c)(3)), and (3) no verification of alarm signal compliance with ANSI standard 1910.165(b). The plan's age is a significant issue: last revised February 2021, no update shown, yet the document's own section 6 commits to annual January review. As of September 2026, an update is now more than five years overdue. The company should have versions from January 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, and 2026 if the stated process was followed. Confidence is medium-high that these gaps and the freshness issue are material.

CASCADE SPECIALTY CHEMICALS, LLC
EMERGENCY ACTION PLAN
Portland Facility, 4410 NW Front Avenue, Portland, Oregon 97210
Revised February 2021
1. Purpose and scope
This Emergency Action Plan describes what employees of Cascade Specialty Chemicals do when there is
a fire, chemical release, medical emergency, earthquake or other emergency at the Portland facility. It
applies to all 42 employees at the Portland facility, including warehouse, drivers, laboratory and office
staff, and to contractors and visitors while on site. The plan is kept in the front office and in the warehouse
break room, and a copy is available to any employee on request.
2. Alarm system
The building has a monitored fire alarm system with audible horns and strobe lights in the warehouse,
laboratory, loading dock and offices. The alarm is monitored 24 hours a day by Cascade Fire & Safety
under a service contract. Manual pull stations are located at each exit door. The alarm is tested on the first
Monday of each month by the facilities lead. A continuous horn means evacuate. Three short horns
repeated means shelter in place because of an outdoor hazard.
3. Evacuation procedures
When the continuous alarm sounds, all employees stop work, secure nothing that requires more than a
few seconds, and leave by the nearest marked exit. Exit routes are posted on the evacuation maps at each
exit door and in Appendix A. Warehouse staff leave by the east dock doors or the north pedestrian door.
Laboratory staff leave by the laboratory's own exterior door on the south wall. Office staff leave by the
main entrance or the west stairwell. Do not use the freight lift. Do not return for belongings.
The assembly point is the far north end of the visitor parking lot, beside the flagpole, at least 150 feet
from the building. Employees assigned as floor wardens (one per area, listed on the warden roster posted
beside each evacuation map) sweep their area, close doors behind them, and report to the assembly point.
For a chemical release outdoors or a hazard that makes leaving the building unsafe, the shelter-in-place
signal sounds. Employees move to the interior conference room or the laboratory corridor, close doors,
and the facilities lead shuts down the building ventilation from the mechanical room panel.
4. Accounting for employees after evacuation
At the assembly point each floor warden takes a headcount of the people from their area against the daily
sign-in sheet and the visitor log, which the receptionist brings out. Any person unaccounted for is reported
at once to the incident coordinator at the assembly point, who passes the information to the fire
department on arrival. No one re-enters the building until the fire department or the incident coordinator
gives the all-clear. Evacuation drills are held twice a year, in spring and autumn.
5. Rescue and medical duties
Employees do not attempt rescue inside the building. First aid is given at the assembly point by the
trained first-aid responders (two per shift, named on the warden roster), who bring the first-aid kit and the
AED from the front office. An employee exposed to a chemical is taken to the emergency shower and
eyewash at the loading dock if it can be reached safely, or to the assembly point, and the SDS for the
product is brought to the responders. Emergency medical services are called for any injury beyond minor
first aid.
6. Training and review
Every new employee is walked through this plan, the exit routes for their work area and the assembly
point on their first day. Floor wardens and first-aid responders are trained annually. The plan is reviewed
with all employees whenever it is changed and whenever an employee's responsibilities under it change.
The facilities lead reviews the plan every January and updates the evacuation maps whenever the building
layout changes.
Appendix A: Evacuation maps (warehouse, laboratory, offices)
Appendix B: Floor warden and first-aid responder roster (posted beside each evacuation map)
